comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C33-C38 regarding DWnt4 mutants recapitulating DFz2/DFz4 phenotypes. Both evaluations find this evidence strongly supported by genetic analyses and morphological data. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Perfect alignment on claims C46-C51 regarding optogenetic behavioral data showing loss of backward locomotion and enhanced forward locomotion in DFz2 KD. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing with appropriate statistical support. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Perfect alignment on claims C52-C55 regarding gentle touch assay data showing shift from backward to turning/forward responses. Both evaluations affirm the evidence strongly supports altered sensorimotor transformation. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Perfect alignment on claims C64-C66 regarding the cooperation model of DFz2 and DFz4 functions. Both evaluations find the model reasonable and supported by functional data, though broader applicability remains speculative. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Strong overlap on claims C19-C22 regarding dendritic changes being minor compared to axonal changes. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of speculation about preserved inputs. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the need for direct observation of downstream activation patterns to strengthen claims about relative contributions.

Strong overlap on claims C15-C16, C23-C24, C27 regarding Bruchpilot co-labeling validating synaptic connections at varicosities. Both evaluations affirm this evidence supports that ectopic projections make functional synaptic connections. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Strong overlap on claims C68-C72 regarding main conclusions linking axon guidance changes to behavioral output. Both evaluations affirm the integration of morphological and behavioral data demonstrates that innervation pattern alterations are sufficient to switch behavioral programs. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Strong overlap on claims C56-C58, C60-C61 regarding conservation of Wnt/Fz signaling across species and filling knowledge gap in Drosophila VNC. Both evaluations support the conservation claims and broader significance, though OpenEval notes 'universal' may be overstated. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Strong overlap on claims C4-C6, C14 regarding DFz2 effects on axon morphology. OpenEval also includes C17-C18 (overexpression data). Both evaluations find the morphological evidence convincing across multiple genetic manipulations. Peer review adds C63 (repulsion model). Both rated SUPPORTED.

Moderate overlap on claims C40-C42 regarding DWnt4 gradient expression. OpenEval focuses on gradient demonstration at transcript and protein levels. Peer review (R4) emphasizes C43-C44 (DFz2 bidirectional gradient) and broader gradient model implications. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Moderate overlap on claims C28-C30 regarding DFz4 KD effects on A6-Wave posterior extension. OpenEval includes C31-C32 (lack of overexpression phenotype). Peer review emphasizes C45 (attractive role) and C62 (repulsion/attraction model). Both rated SUPPORTED.

Moderate overlap on claims C78-C80 regarding suppression mechanisms for anterior projections. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes speculation. Peer review (R18) groups with C75-C77 (synapse formation mechanisms) and affirms overall logic without challenging specific mechanisms. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Moderate overlap on claims C81-C84 regarding evolutionary implications. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation beyond the data. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming the evolutionary interpretation as providing 'entry point to understand behavioral adaptations during evolution.' Divergent evaluation types reflect different standards for evolutionary claims.

Both address claim C96 regarding potential confounding effects of p-Wave alterations. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting this caveat is acknowledged but not directly addressed. Both recognize this as an unresolved alternative explanation.

Moderate overlap on claims C10-C13 regarding segment-specific differences in Wave neurons. OpenEval also includes C1-C3 (broader biological context). Both evaluations accept these as well-established foundational observations from prior work. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on claims C75-C77 regarding synapse formation mechanisms. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes direct connectivity data would strengthen claims. Peer review groups with C78-C80 and affirms overall mechanistic logic. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on claims C43-C44 regarding DFz2 bidirectional gradient and repulsion/attraction model. OpenEval also includes C62-C63. Peer review (R4) emphasizes broader gradient implications with C40-C42. Both find the model reasonable and supported. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on claims C88-C89 regarding developmental identification of Wave neurons. OpenEval also includes C90-C91. Both evaluations accept this as important methodological validation. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claim C9 regarding evolutionary flexibility. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes some overstatement. Peer review explicitly supports evolutionary interpretation. OpenEval also addresses C8 (conservation), which peer review groups with C56-C58, C60-C61, C87 in R10.

Both address claim C45 regarding DFz4 attractive role. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes incomplete characterization due to lack of DFz4 expression data. Peer review groups with C28-C30, C62 and affirms the attractive role interpretation. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claims C73-C74 regarding how axon rerouting leads to functional changes. OpenEval includes C75-C77 (synapse formation) and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer review groups C73-C74 with C68-C72 (main conclusions) and affirms the mechanistic interpretation. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claims C31-C32 regarding lack of DFz4 overexpression phenotype. OpenEval groups with C28-C30 (DFz4 KD effects). Peer review groups with C17-C18 (DFz2 overexpression) as complementary gain-of-function data. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claims C17-C18 regarding DFz2 overexpression effects. OpenEval groups with C4-C6, C14 (DFz2 KD morphology). Peer review groups with C31-C32 as gain-of-function complement to loss-of-function data. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claims C25-C26 regarding Bruchpilot labeling methodology. OpenEval groups with C15-C16, C23-C24, C27 (synaptic validation). Peer review focuses specifically on C25-C26, C92 as methodological validation. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claim C92 regarding varicosity observations. OpenEval groups with C93 as minor methodological points. Peer review groups with C25-C26 as synaptic marker validation. Both rated SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claim C7 regarding main conclusion about circuit diversification. OpenEval groups with C68-C72. Peer review groups with C55, C85-C86 emphasizing overarching significance. Both rated SUPPORTED.

OpenEval addresses claim C67 regarding prior work on input connectivity changes affecting behavior. This citation provides context but is not directly evaluated by peer reviewers. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval addresses claim C94 regarding mechanistic interpretation of increased turning response. This speculative inference about circuit mechanisms is not directly addressed by peer reviewers. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of speculation.

OpenEval addresses claims C97-C105 regarding broader scientific context and knowledge gaps motivating the study. These standard introduction/background statements are not directly evaluated by peer reviewers. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED.
